hormonal_therapy.name: Tamoxifen
hormonal_therapy.mechanism: Blocks estrogen receptors in breast tissue, preventing estrogen from fueling cancer cell growth.
hormonal_therapy.plain_english: Tells estrogen to stop feeding the cancer cells.

hormonal_therapy.name: Anastrozole
hormonal_therapy.mechanism: Blocks aromatase enzyme that converts androgens to estrogen, dropping estrogen to near zero.
hormonal_therapy.plain_english: Shuts off the body's estrogen factory so it can't feed the cancer.

hormonal_therapy.name: Letrozole
hormonal_therapy.mechanism: Blocks aromatase enzyme, reducing estrogen production by >99%.
hormonal_therapy.plain_english: Nearly eliminates estrogen so the cancer has nothing to grow on.

hormonal_therapy.name: Exemestane
hormonal_therapy.mechanism: Irreversibly inactivates aromatase, permanently blocking that enzyme.
hormonal_therapy.plain_english: Permanently disables the enzyme that makes estrogen.

hormonal_therapy.name: Fulvestrant
hormonal_therapy.mechanism: Degrades estrogen receptors entirely rather than just blocking them.
hormonal_therapy.plain_english: Destroys the cancer's estrogen antenna so it can't receive the signal at all.

targeted_therapy.name: Trastuzumab
targeted_therapy.mechanism: Attaches to HER2 protein on cancer cells and flags them for immune destruction.
targeted_therapy.plain_english: Puts a target on HER2-positive cancer cells so your immune system can find and kill them.

targeted_therapy.name: Pertuzumab
targeted_therapy.mechanism: Blocks a different part of HER2 than trastuzumab — used together they hit two sites.
targeted_therapy.plain_english: Works with Herceptin to block HER2 from two angles at once.

targeted_therapy.name: T-DM1 (Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine)
targeted_therapy.mechanism: Trastuzumab carrying a chemotherapy payload directly into HER2+ cells.
targeted_therapy.plain_english: A guided missile — Herceptin finds the HER2 cancer cells and delivers chemo directly inside them.

targeted_therapy.name: T-DXd (Trastuzumab Deruxtecan)
targeted_therapy.mechanism: Next-generation antibody-drug conjugate with a more potent payload and bystander effect.
targeted_therapy.plain_english: An upgraded guided missile that also affects nearby cancer cells — works even in HER2-low tumors.

targeted_therapy.name: Palbociclib
targeted_therapy.mechanism: Blocks CDK4 and CDK6 proteins that tell cancer cells to divide.
targeted_therapy.plain_english: Puts the brakes on cancer cell division — they can't multiply as fast.

targeted_therapy.name: Ribociclib
targeted_therapy.mechanism: Same mechanism as palbociclib with demonstrated overall survival benefit.
targeted_therapy.plain_english: Same brake on cell division as Ibrance, with proven survival improvement.

targeted_therapy.name: Olaparib
targeted_therapy.mechanism: Blocks PARP enzymes that help repair DNA — BRCA-mutated cancer cells can't survive without them.
targeted_therapy.plain_english: Removes the cancer's backup DNA repair system. BRCA-mutated cells can't fix themselves and die.

targeted_therapy.name: Abemaciclib
targeted_therapy.mechanism: CDK4/6 inhibitor used in both adjuvant and metastatic settings.
targeted_therapy.plain_english: Brakes on cancer cell division — approved for use even before cancer spreads in high-risk patients.

targeted_therapy.name: Sacituzumab Govitecan
targeted_therapy.mechanism: Delivers chemo directly into Trop-2 expressing cells (high in TNBC).
targeted_therapy.plain_english: A guided missile specifically designed for triple-negative breast cancer.

targeted_therapy.name: Pembrolizumab
targeted_therapy.mechanism: Removes the 'don't attack me' signal cancer uses to hide from the immune system.
targeted_therapy.plain_english: Unmasks cancer cells so your immune system can see and attack them.

chemotherapy.name: Doxorubicin
chemotherapy.mechanism: Damages DNA in rapidly dividing cells.
chemotherapy.plain_english: Breaks DNA in fast-growing cells — cancer cells divide fast so they're hit hardest.

chemotherapy.name: Paclitaxel
chemotherapy.mechanism: Locks the cell division machinery so cancer cells can't finish dividing and die.
chemotherapy.plain_english: Freezes cancer cells mid-division so they can't reproduce.

chemotherapy.name: Docetaxel
chemotherapy.mechanism: Same as paclitaxel but different formulation and dosing schedule.
chemotherapy.plain_english: Same mechanism as Taxol — freezes cell division.

chemotherapy.name: Cyclophosphamide
chemotherapy.mechanism: Cross-links DNA strands so cancer cells can't replicate.
chemotherapy.plain_english: Jams cancer cell DNA so it can't make copies of itself.

chemotherapy.name: Capecitabine
chemotherapy.mechanism: Converted to 5-FU inside cells, blocking DNA synthesis.
chemotherapy.plain_english: An oral chemo pill that becomes active inside tumor cells.

common_regimens.name: AC-T
common_regimens.schedule: AC every 3 weeks x4 → T every 3 weeks x4 (or weekly x12)

common_regimens.name: TCHP
common_regimens.schedule: Every 3 weeks x6 → complete HP x1 year

common_regimens.name: Keytruda + chemo → Keytruda
common_regimens.schedule: Pembrolizumab + chemo neoadjuvant → surgery → pembrolizumab x9 cycles
